sessions.feedback: Nothing blocked me this session. Two suggestions. (1) read_page failed on CNBC and Investing.com URLs, so I got the article text from web_search results instead; a note on which domains read_page can fetch would help. (2) A screener-style tool listing the largest idiosyncratic moves (versus industry) across all eligible stocks, including after-hours, would find catalysts faster than the digest's top-20 list, which is dominated by thin pre-market prints (100 to 1,000 shares). Stops and targets are fixed at entry, so I could not tell which stop width suits the volatility; the stop sat 0.7% below the close in a 3%-a-day tape, and I only fixed it through extend.

It is unclear whether a stop that gaps through (NVDA pre-market 141 versus a 144.88 stop) fills at the stop price or at the open price. Documenting that would help me size positions and decide whether to close manually. Otherwise nothing blocked me.

No blockers this session. Suggestions: (1) the digest's pre-market mover list is dominated by thin prints (e.g. OCSL at 200 shares), so a filter on a minimum share count or dollar volume would help. (2) The scan tool's earnings field says 'time not given' for most names, so a before-open/after-close flag would help judge whether a move already includes the earnings reaction (PANW's +9.9% regular-session move looked like earnings but came before the report). (3) A ticker-level 'consensus vs actual' feed would save web searches.

The NVDA CNBC article could not be fetched with read_page. The news tool sometimes labels stories misleadingly: the digest said "SEC investigation" for NVDA, but the cited MarketWatch page did not mention one. The helper answers are useful for checking claims. Reports on GLBE conflicted (+8% vs -12% pre) and cannot be checked from pre-market tools alone. A consensus-vs-actual field in scan would save web searches.

The data was sufficient. Pre-market prints on thin volume (e.g. ESLT +8% on 605 shares, ACM, KNX) are hard to trust, so a pre-market VWAP or a bid/ask indication would help judge the likely opening price. The read_page helper often returns only teasers for paywalled pages, so a way to fetch the SEC exhibit text directly would help. Consensus estimates were not available from the tools and I had to use web search for them.
No blocking issues. A premarket movers list in the digest (not only previous-session movers) would help since orders fill at the open.
No VIX or futures data in tools; would help judge the volatility regime.

summary:
Session 2026-11-23.

Session 2026-11-23 (pre-open). Context: 11-20 was a capitulation day. SPY -3.64% (7th straight loss, 151M shares, -10% from its high), QQQ -5.67%, XLK -7.3%, VIX 35.9, NVDA -14% to 125.5. Pre-market is a sharp rebound: SPY +2.7%, QQQ +3.6%, NVDA +8.5% (Trump wants Huang reinstated; Bessent left the door open and warned the Fed against over-tightening; Asian state support). The Fed hike on Dec 9 is still ~90% priced, with a 50bp hike possible. Michigan 1y inflation expectations fell to 3.7%.
Portfolio: all three stop-outs are settled (NVDA -10.0%, ESLT -10.2%, P -12.2%). Only AS remains, at 6.6% (cost 30.53, close 28.27). Cash is 93%. Equity is $97.4k, about -2.6% since 10-29, against SPY about -10%, so cash is winning.
Decision: extended AS with a wider stop (10% below today's fill, about 26), a 16% target and a 10-day horizon, because the old 28.06 stop was inside one normal daily move. No new trades.
Examined and skipped: CRWD buying ZS (all-stock, 1.135 CRWD per ZS, spread only ~1.3%); UNH/HUM/CVS (-4 to -6% pre on the CMS Star Ratings proposal, which affects 2031 payments and is roughly priced, low beta); NVDA re-entry (CA probe widened, closed-door Huang session 12-01, Senate hearing 12-03, binary); P and ESLT re-entry (no base, gap-up in a whipsaw tape); INTU (-12.8%, FY guide cut); DELL (earnings 11-24 AMC); GPN (takeover exploration, priced). Buying a +2.7% gap in a market that whipsawed on 11-19 is a coin flip, not an edge.
Check next session: how the 11-23 bounce closed (hold or fade); QQQ higher low above 11-20 (~596 intraday) and VIX below ~28 as a stabilisation signal; the AS open and the new stop; the DELL print (11-24 AMC), ADSK and ZM reactions; the NVDA/Bessent answer ~11-26; Thanksgiving 11-26 (closed) and 11-27 (early close). Look for beat-and-raise names that did not gap, with idiosyncratic alpha.
notes:
Session log (condensed)
S1-S9 (10-29 to 11-16): all cash through an AI/tech rout and hot-CPI/Fed-hike repricing (INTC -25%, NOW -27%, FTNT -20% on a beat/raise, RDDT -29%, Huang resignation at NVDA). Falling knives kept falling (FTNT, INTC 11-03). Catalyst moves in biotech/M&A are priced by the open (TU, CGON, SMMT, SLS, ADT).
S10 (11-17): long AS 7% (beat/raise/$1B buyback, 5 down days into print) and long ESLT 5% (beat, record backlog), stops 8%/10%.
S11 (11-18): long NVDA 6% after blowout (rev 115.8B vs 109B, guide 130B, +$150B buyback), stop 9%.
S12 (11-19): long P 4% after +51% revenue beat/raise. Same day: Anthropic IPO, QQQ +2.1% pre then -2.2% close (whipsaw).
S13 (11-20): held all; NVDA gapped through stop.
Outcomes: NVDA stop -10.0% (filled ~143; it closed 11-20 at 125.5, -14% on the day, so honouring the stop saved ~11 points), ESLT stop -10.2%, P stop -12.2%. All three beat-and-raise drift longs lost 10-12% within 1-3 days. AS is open, -7%.
S14 (11-23): 11-20 was a capitulation day: SPY -3.64% (7th straight loss, 151M shares, -10% from high), QQQ -5.67% (briefly -20% from the Oct 6 high), XLK -7.3%, VIX 35.9 (highest since March). NVDA -14%. Pre-market 11-23: SPY +2.7%, QQQ +3.6%, NVDA +8.5% on Trump pushing Huang's reinstatement, Asian state support (Korea stabilisation fund, China ETF buying), Bessent warning the Fed on over-tightening. Fed hike Dec 9 (25bp ~90%+, 50bp possible; Waller backs 50). Michigan 1y inflation expectations fell to 3.7% from 4.7%. Held AS only (6.6% of equity, cash 93%). Skipped: CRWD/ZS (CRWD buys ZS all-stock, 1.135 CRWD per ZS; the arb spread is only ~1.3%, no edge), UNH (-6% pre on the CMS Star Ratings proposal that hits 2031 payments; priced roughly fairly, low beta, no edge), NVDA re-entry (binary political events), P/ESLT re-entry (no stabilisation, gap-up in a whipsaw tape), INTU (-12.8%, FY guide cut, software de-rating), DELL (earnings 11-24 AMC, binary).
Lessons (cite trades):
1. Beat-and-raise drift longs fail when macro beta dominates (NVDA, P, ESLT 11-17 to 11-20; ROST/INTU also sold off on beats). Do not add them while QQQ is making new lows; wait for a higher low and falling VIX.
2. Honour stops in a rout; do not override (NVDA: the stop saved ~11 more points). But stops must be sized to the vol regime: with SPY moving 3%/day, an 8-10% stop on a 4-6% daily-vol stock sits inside 2 sigma. Size smaller (3-4%) or use wider stops with smaller weight. AS's old stop of 28.06 was 0.7% below the close; I widened it to 10% on 11-23.
3. Gap risk: a stop is not a guarantee; NVDA filled -10.0% vs -9.1% stop, P -12.2% vs ~-12% planned, because of pre-market gaps.
4. Pre-market strength in a bear tape is not tradable (CRWV 11-11; QQQ +2.1% pre then -2.2% on 11-19). Buying an opening gap-up of +2.7% means paying for most of the rebound. The cash position is currently winning versus SPY (equity -2.6% vs SPY -10% since 10-29), so cash needs a real edge to be replaced.
5. A long beats SPY only with idiosyncratic alpha; a beta bounce bet is a pure market-timing coin flip (about 0.5 probability), not a high-probability trade.
6. Retail earnings include IEEPA tariff-refund benefits - use adjusted numbers (LOW, WSM, TGT).
7. Sympathy gap-ups (cyber peers after PANW, SPXC etc.) are not trades. Thin pre-market prints (<1% of avg volume) are unreliable.
8. Merger arb on all-stock deals: check the spread before getting excited (ZS +20% pre vs 1.135 x CRWD gives a ~1.3% spread).

prompt:
Your universe is every eligible US stock. Your style is a few high-quality trades.

- Look for situations where recent, specific information has not yet been reflected in the price:
  earnings surprises and guidance changes, contracts, regulatory decisions, management changes,
  supply problems, sector-wide shocks. Remember you trade at the open, after the overnight reaction,
  so ask what is still left to move, not what already moved. It works in both directions: bad
  news the price has not finished absorbing is a short.
- Prefer clear catalysts you can verify over vague narratives. A strong case beats a busy portfolio,
  so concentrate on your best ideas. Cash is the right answer when thorough research has turned up
  nothing, and only then.
- Size positions by conviction and by how much could go wrong. Set stops and targets you would
  actually stand behind.
- Use the movers and most-active lists as places to start looking, not as reasons to buy.
